cases.assertion: For every valid textual identifier id, binary_to_text(text_to_binary(id)) must equal id byte-for-byte.
For every valid 17-byte binary input b, text_to_binary(binary_to_text(b)) must equal b byte-for-byte.
All invalid-string corpus inputs must be rejected by strict string conversion. A boolean predicate is only required if exposed.
All invalid-binary corpus inputs must be rejected by strict binary conversion.
For valid identifiers with unequal timestamps, both unsigned binary and ASCII lexicographic comparisons match timestamp order.
Within the same second ordering follows randomness, not call order; compare unsigned binary and canonical ASCII.
Repeated generation produces valid 26 ASCII Base36 identifiers whose timestamps fall between wall-clock seconds before/after call (allow documented clock-tolerance policy).
Audit all normal generation code paths to verify a secure OS/runtime CSPRNG supplies 12 bytes, with no weak random fallback. Statistical tests cannot prove cryptographic security.
If the entropy source can be fault-injected, ensure generation fails closed rather than continuing with weak or reused randomness.
Only if caller-supplied timestamp generation exists: returned timestamp must equal requested second; boundary timestamps must succeed and out-of-range seconds must be rejected.
Only if a direct binary generation API exists: each output is 17 bytes and text/binary round trips succeed.
Only if a parser exists: it returns a lossless integer timestamp and original 12 randomness bytes or lowercase 24-hex value.
Only if a datetime is returned: it denotes the exact UTC second, not local-time interpretation.
Only if full boolean validation is exposed: all valid vectors yield true, invalid-string vectors false.
Only if a format-only predicate exists: it accepts shape-valid entropy overflow strings as well-formed, but does not imply full validity.
